description_full: Nexxen International Ltd. provides end-to-end and video-first platform that engages advertising campaigns for brands, agencies, media groups, and content creators worldwide. It offers demand side platform, which provides a self-service solution for advertisers and their agencies to plan, activate, and manage omni-channel campaigns, access to inventory, data for audience targeting, AI planning capabilities across formats, testing solutions and reporting and management; Data Platform, provides insights and recommendations across geographic, behavioral, consumption, and demographic data, as well as enables advertisers and publishers to directly onboard, manage, plan, activate, and measure, with data from multiple sources to optimize performance and ROI; and Supply Side Platform, a self-service supply side platforms solution for publishers to sell their digital advertising inventory through a real-time bidding auction across screens, including mobile devices, CTVs, streaming devices, and desktop. The company also provides analytics and artificial intelligence services; Nexxen Discovery, an audience insight and activation product to o help customers create targeted segments, extend reach, and optimize campaigns real time; and Nexxen Studio, an in-house digital creative studio offers various creative solutions to tailored to needs of brands and agencies. It serves ad buyers, including brands and agencies, and digital publishers. The company has a strategic partnership with L2 Data to launch VoterMatch, a platform for political advertisers. The company was formerly known as Tremor International Ltd and changed its name to Nexxen International Ltd. in January 2024. Nexxen International Ltd. was incorporated in 2007 and is headquartered in Tel Aviv-Yafo, Israel.

financial_summary: Nexxen International Ltd. is a small-cap communication services business with a $503M market cap on $365M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +3% over the past three years, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory. Operating margins are contracting by -3.2pp, the first warning that competitive pressure is eroding the franchise.
Returns on capital run at 8% against a 11% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests.

The business throws off $98M in free cash flow — roughly 27 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 4.40× so those profits are backed by real cash.
Accruals are elevated at -11.3% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 15× is fortress-like.

Management returns a meaningful 20.2% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 10% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and profit capture is only 0.4× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
